question.text: Under Regulation 91E of LODR, an NPO that is only REGISTERED on a Social Stock Exchange (without raising funds through it) may continue registration without raising funds for a maximum period of:

answer.text: One year from the date of registration.
Five years, extendable for a further two years by the SSE.
Three years from the date of registration.
Two years from the date of registration.

explanation.text: The Logic: Regulation 91E provides that a NPO registered on SSE shall be permitted NOT to raise funds through it for a maximum period of TWO years from the date of registration; upon expiry, the NPO must have at least one listed project failing which it shall cease to be registered. The Trap: One year / three years / five years are common distractors. The two-year ceiling is the regulatory trigger for de-registration if no listed project materialises. Cross-Exam Context: XXIII Topic 6 (Registration and Listing) and this Topic 9 (Disclosure) both lean on the two-year sunset. III-A compliance will not have this - it is SSE-specific. Assessor's Pro-Tip: Track the two-year clock per NPO client starting from the SSE registration date. A SIA's planning deck for any Year-2 NPO should include a decision tree: raise ZCZP (stay listed) vs exit and re-apply later.
